claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has been reported in a hierarchical heterostructured state with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Local chemical-environment descriptors can be extracted from imaging or compositional mapping of HfNbTiVAl10.
A machine-learning surrogate can be trained on a limited set of coarse-grained simulations and experimental data.
The proposed surrogate can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Multilevel chemical fluctuations and hierarchical phase boundaries mediate stress distribution and failure modes.
The stiffness, yield behavior, and toughness of HfNbTiVAl10 are governed by its chemical heterogeneity.
Reduced descriptors of chemical fluctuations can retain the critical microstructural influences on macroscopic mechanical properties.
Using reduced descriptors allows the surrogate to bypass the computational demands of full atomistic or CALPHAD methods.
The method will improve prediction accuracy by approximately 10–20% over the stated baseline methods.
The method will provide a computational-efficiency gain of roughly 3–5 times over full first-principles or CALPHAD-based methods.
Prior first-principles, CALPHAD, and high-fidelity machine-learning studies on similar alloy systems provide accuracy and efficiency baselines.
The method may lose reliability when processed HfNbTiVAl10 deviates significantly from the characterized hierarchical heterostructure.
The emergence of unexpected intermetallic phases may make the method unreliable.
Descriptor values outside the training-data range may make the surrogate unreliable.
Analogous high-entropy and complex-alloy systems provide preliminary support for the predicted accuracy and efficiency gains.
Validation should use room-temperature tensile and fracture tests on samples replicating the reported hierarchical microstructure.
The framework is falsified if it fails both to achieve at least a threefold efficiency improvement and to improve prediction accuracy by at least 10% relative to baseline methods.
